Hi Jane —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the templates. High level answers first, then I’ll attach a one-paragraph billing note for procurement you can use.

1) PO line-iteming for per-token usage: Redwood bills hosted API usage on a per-token basis by default. For POs, customers commonly do either:
   - Option A: Put a committed monthly spend as a single line item (e.g., $X/month) which we treat as a prepay/commit that unlocks a blended discounted per-token rate. Overage is billed monthly at the agreed overage per-token rate.
   - Option B: Put expected usage estimated by month and reference our per-token rate table; we invoice actual tokens monthly. This keeps flexibility but provides less predictable spend.

2) Vendor form fields: yes, we can populate the vendor form. We will need the exact remit address and your billing contact. We can provide W-9 and insurance certs.

3) Commit to unlock tiers: We can do both — start on pure usage and convert to a commit with retroactive tiering within a defined window, or agree to an initial committed tier to secure a lower blended rate. For procurement ease, most customers prefer Option A.

I’ve drafted a short procurement note below you can paste into the PO system. If procurement prefers, we can also fill your vendor form and return it as a signed PDF.

[Procurement billing note]
Redwood Inference (Redwood) provides hosted API inference billed on a per-token basis. Acme Retail and Redwood may agree to a committed monthly spend (line item) which is applied as a prepayment at a discounted blended per-token rate; any monthly usage above the committed token equivalent will be billed at the agreed overage per-token rate. Invoices are issued monthly and due net 30. Redwood will provide W-9, insurance certificates, and a completed vendor form upon request.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll fill your vendor form and return as a PDF (ETA: tomorrow).
- Marissa (CC) will draft a simple SOW/attachment for the PO if you need service-level language.
- If procurement wants a short call to walk the PO fields, happy to schedule 30 mins.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt

On Mon, Sep 14, 2026 at 11:00 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) PO line-iteming for per-token usage: Redwood bills hosted API usage on a per-token basis by default.
> 2) Vendor form fields: yes, we can populate the vendor form.
> 3) Commit to unlock tiers: We can do both — start on pure usage and convert to a commit with retroactive tiering within a defined window

Hannah — thanks for the clarity. A couple of procurement constraints to flag up front so we avoid back-and-forth:

- Our finance team requires a line-itemed monthly spend for budgetary reconciliation. We cannot process a PO that references an abstract per-token table unless there is a committed line-item (we can accept a committed credit and still track tokens separately).
- Preferred vendor form must include: vendor remit address, EIN/tax id, bank wiring instructions, and a contact for invoice disputes. The attached form will be rejected if those fields are left blank.
- We typically do not accept retroactive tiering exceptions after the fact. If you propose a conversion from usage to commit, it needs to be effective the start of the next billing period.
- Our standard PO terms are Net 45 for first-time vendors unless a faster cadence is justified by procurement leadership.

From our side, the simplest path to close quickly is:
1) Redwood provides a completed vendor form with all fields filled (including W-9 and insurance).
2) We issue a PO with a committed monthly line item (number and $ amount) that maps to a token-equivalent.
3) Both parties sign an SOW that references the per-token overage rates and how the committed credit is reconciled monthly.

If Redwood is unable to accept a committed line-item on the PO, we can escalate to finance, but that will add 1–2 weeks. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a committed monthly credit on the PO that maps to a blended rate, with overage billing as described?

Thanks —
Acme Vendor Forms Team
Attachments: none

Thanks — that’s helpful and understood. We can accommodate the flow you outlined. To keep this moving, here’s the proposed compromise that satisfies your finance constraints while preserving usage economics:

Proposal:
- Acme issues a committed monthly credit line item on the PO (e.g., $50,000/month) for an initial 3-month term.
- Redwood will convert that dollar commit to a token-equivalent at execution using the agreed blended per-token rate and apply that credit monthly against actual token usage.
- Any usage above the committed token-equivalent will be invoiced monthly at the overage per-token rate. Overage invoices will include token counts and per-token math for reconciliation.
- Conversion from pure usage to a committed line item is allowed but must be effective the start of the next billing period (we accept your constraint). Retroactive crediting outside that window is not standard but can be reviewed by finance for edge cases.
- Payment terms: we are agreeable to Net 45 on first PO for Acme; subsequent POs can be Net 30.

Next steps (I’ll action these today):
- I’m attaching the vendor form filled with Redwood’s remit address, tax id, bank details, and a billing contact (redwood_vendor-form-filled.pdf).
- Marissa (CC) attached a short SOW that can be appended to your PO (Acme_SOW_Redwood.pdf).
- If you want, schedule a 30-minute call to finalize amounts and a signing cadence — otherwise, confirm committed $ amount and we’ll return a countersigned vendor form and SOW.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
